recommendation: Keep the source change. It aligns the active Observation narrative with the current StructureDefinition and avoids reintroducing the choice-type binding confusion that FHIR-8479 and FHIR-8477 addressed.
issue_request: FHIR-8479 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request from DSTU1 asking to remove the example binding from Observation.value[x] because it caused profiling problems for choice-type values, while preserving the intent in narrative text.
initial_application: Git commit 861e258d1a removed the ObservationValue binding rows from the historical Observation spreadsheet source and added explanatory Observation notes text. The current StructureDefinition source for Observation.value[x] has no binding block, so the formal removal remained applied.
additional_context: FHIR-8477 records the underlying methodology problem for bindings on choice-type elements such as Observation.value[x]. FHIR-22801 later touched only a typo in the same Observation notes sentence. Observation is active in source/fhir.ini, and community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: Changed source/observation/observation-notes.xml to replace the sentence saying valueCodeableConcept is bound with wording that coded values can come from SNOMED CT or local result codes. This keeps the explanatory intent while matching the deliberately unbound ElementDefinition.
source_changes: source/observation/observation-notes.xml: rewrote the coded-result sentence in the Using codes in Observation.value section to avoid saying the unbound valueCodeableConcept element is formally bound.
